explanation: A special occasion or festival dedicated to honoring God and celebrating his works.
A weekly day of rest to honor God, usually observed from sunset on Friday to sunset on Saturday.
An important Jewish feast that celebrates the deliverance of the people of Israel from slavery in Egypt under the leadership of Moses.
A seven-day festival that follows Passover, where Jews eat unleavened bread (matzah) to remember their hasty departure from Egypt.
A religious ceremony in which the first and best fruits and vegetables from the harvest were offered to God as thanks for his blessings.
A Jewish feast celebrated 50 days after Passover, also known as Shavuot. It marks the time when God gave the Torah to Moses on Mount Sinai.
A seven-day feast, also known as Sukkot, celebrated in autumn to remember Israel's 40 years of wandering in the wilderness and God's protection.
A Jewish holy day, also known as the Day of Atonement, where Jews ask for forgiveness for their sins and fast for 25 hours.
